newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Archer Daniels buys Jamaica Flour Mills control.
newsitem.headline: Archer Daniels buys Jamaica Flour Mills control.

text.p: Major shareholders in Jamaica Flour Mills announced Thursday they had agreed to sell a controlling interest to Archer Daniels Midland Co's ADM Milling, ending weeks of acrimonious bickering over the buyout bid for Jamaica's only flour mill.
Major shareholders agreed to sell 51 percent of Jamaica Flour equity to ADM, the shareholders said in a statement.

Earlier this year, ADM offered $35 million for 100 percent of Jamaica Flour, which is traded on the Kingston exchange. Following complaints that the offer was less than half book value of the company, the offer was raised to $40.7 million.

However, the company's managers complained that the offer did not take into account the approximately $20 million Jamaica Flour was likely to receive as a result of a court decision regarding insurance payouts for damages resulting from an explosion at the mills in 1988, nor did it take into account Jamaica Flour's $10 million in cash reserves.
ADM had also given assurances that while the jobs of existing employees were safe, the same could not be said for managers.

Following talks Tuesday and Wednesday, ADM upped its offer to $42.3 million for 100 percent of Jamaica Flour. It also agreed to management's demand that 80 percent of the insurance proceeds, after tax, be paid out to shareholders and that the existing management be retained, officials said.
Having obtained control of the company, ADM must now make the same offer to other shareholders. The company has all along stated it intends to obtain all of Jamaica Flour's shares.
